$comment: Findings that do not fail the run (scripts/security-report.mjs). Each entry names the tool, the id of the finding (a CVE, a rule), optionally a part of its location (where), why and until when (YYYY-MM-DD): after that date it fails the run again and must be looked at once more. "kind": "false-positive": not a vulnerability of this code (the tool is wrong, or the flagged flow is intended and safe: the reason says why); without kind: an accepted risk, a real weakness kept for the reason given. The report counts both apart from the open findings.

risks.reason: the last user is root: see the findings Missing User Instruction (KICS) and DS-0002 (Trivy config) of the same image
the last user is root: see the findings Missing User Instruction (KICS) and DS-0002 (Trivy config) of the same image
the modules are pinned: go get takes the versions of LEGO_VERSION, LEGO_UPGRADES and GO_UPGRADES (variables hadolint does not read), go build then builds what go.mod pins
control is a named build context (--build-context control=nginxions/backend/nginxions/control), not a stage
NPMplus starts as root and drops to PUID/PGID itself; the container runs with cap_drop ALL, one capability (SETGID) and no-new-privileges (see the KICS finding Missing User Instruction)
the nano agent of open-appsec runs as root as upstream does (its shared memory and IPC with the attachment of nginx); its own services listen on 127.0.0.1 only
the development image (compose.dev.yaml), never published

the interface of the test stack has a certificate of a root CA the test creates in the PKI of NginxionS (DAST has no public CA in a closed network); a root of an administrator is trusted by the clients they give it to. testssl.sh checks the chain from that root (--add-ca)
a CAA record is a record of the DNS of the domain of the administrator, not of NginxionS; the test stack has no DNS (a closed network) and its names have no zone
BREACH needs a secret in the body of a compressed response next to text an attacker sends; the API takes its token from a cookie and a header and does not reflect it in compressed bodies
private addresses in the examples of the API schema (/api/schema) and in answers about the hosts of the administrator (upstream addresses): data of the interface, behind its login
addresses in the code of the interface (examples and defaults of forms): text of the bundle, not data
the test site behind dast.local (whoami) echoes the addresses of the request: the site, not NginxionS
Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is for the site behind the proxy host to send (the test site whoami); it can be added per host in its advanced configuration
Unix times in answers (created_on, expiry of certificates): data of the interface, not a disclosure
numbers of the bundle of the interface that look like Unix times
ZAP sends requests the schema does not describe (methods and types it guesses); the API answers them with its JSON error, not with the type ZAP expects
performance advice of gixy (open_file_cache), no security effect
MIT: the package.json of the package has no license field, its LICENSE file is the MIT license (Brian White); a dependency of express-fileupload (uploads of NPMplus)
MIT: the package.json of the package has no license field, its LICENSE file is the MIT license (Brian White); a dependency of express-fileupload (uploads of NPMplus)
not a stored password hash: the id of the CrowdSec machine is derived from its random 256-bit password so that a new password is a new machine; the password itself is never stored hashed

not installed: pip ships an SBOM of its vendored code (pip/_vendor/bom.cdx.json) that names setuptools 70.3.0 as the source of its pkg_resources; the setuptools of the image is 84.2.1, and the flaw is in a part pkg_resources does not have (PackageIndex)
nginx of NginxionS is built with AWS-LC, which knows X25519MLKEM768: the post-quantum group does not stop nginx (it starts in every test)
gixy cannot resolve the cipher selectors of the configuration; testssl.sh checks the ciphers nginx really offers (dast.local:443) and finds none weak
nothing is created: the file the agent generated in its own /tmp (/tmp/local_appsec.policy) is opened read only (flag "r") and parsed as JSON; a missing file is reported as no policy

the path of a host's configuration is built from a host type every caller passes as a constant (proxy_host, redirection_host, dead_host, stream, default) and the integer id of its database row; nothing of a request reaches it
the cookie holds the session token itself, as every login does: signed, httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, __Host- prefix
the condition only rejects an empty token; every other token goes through jwt.verify with the public key
the length of the code chooses how it is checked: 6 digits by TOTP, 8 characters against the bcrypt hashes of the backup codes; any other length is refused, both checks throw on a mismatch
cert_id is the integer id of a certificate row in the URL path, not a certificate or a key: CodeQL takes any name with "cert" for secret data
certificate_id and expand are the id of a row and the names of related objects, not secrets: CodeQL takes any name with "cert" for secret data
the Gravatar download: NginxionS fixes DISABLE_GRAVATAR=true (docs/ENV-INVENTORY.md), so the branch does not run; the file name is a sha256 and the extension one of png, jpeg, gif
the block page is what the administrator configures (WAF -> Block page), rendered with escaping into its own fixed file
a CSR the administrator uploads is stored for its certificate (a directory 0700 per certificate id) or checked by openssl in a private temporary directory
the log of a failed ACME request is written, with the secrets redacted, to its fixed file for "Full log"
a hub snapshot the administrator uploads, or hub files downloaded on the administrator's request: paths are checked by safeRel (normalized, no .., not absolute), archives may hold plain files only
the GeoIP database the administrator uploads is checked by the reader before it replaces the file (a fixed path, written as .tmp and renamed)
inputs of openssl written as 0600 files of a private temporary directory, removed afterwards
the credentials NginxionS reads from its secrets volume are sent to the local CrowdSec LAPI they belong to (internal network)
the token of nginxions-control, read from the secrets volume, is sent to nginxions-control on 127.0.0.1 only

the Docker socket is for nginxions-control alone (System -> Services): a whitelist of operations on containers labelled nginxions.managed, a token, an audit log, 127.0.0.1 only; the container nginxions, which takes traffic from the internet, has no socket (CLAUDE.md, Security)
the sensitive host path is the Docker socket of nginxions-control, see the finding Docker Socket Mounted In Container
see the Semgrep finding missing-user-entrypoint: the agent runs as root as upstream does

NPMplus starts as root and drops to PUID/PGID itself; NginxionS keeps PUID 0 for now (docs/ENV-INVENTORY.md) but runs the container with cap_drop ALL, one capability (SETGID) and no-new-privileges. A non-root PUID needs the start script to work without CHOWN/SETUID: open work, see docs/DEVSECOPS.md
the development image (compose.dev.yaml), never published

KICS lists every cap_add to be checked: every service drops ALL; nginxions adds SETGID only (nginx, root, sets the groups of its workers; the ports need no capability, sysctls of openappsec), postgres the five its entrypoint needs to give its data directory to the user postgres (CHOWN, DAC_OVERRIDE, FOWNER, SETUID, SETGID)
test-upstream (traefik/whoami) is an image from scratch without a shell or any program to run a check; every other service of the overlays has its healthcheck
test-upstream (traefik/whoami) is an image from scratch without a shell or any program to run a check; every other service of the overlays has its healthcheck

the versions are pinned where KICS does not look: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile installs the lockfile of the frontend and of the backend; the dev image installs the version each dependency has in package.json

Alpine keeps only the current version of a package in its repositories: a pinned apk version breaks the build at the next security update. The base images are pinned by digest and Renovate raises them; the images are scanned (Trivy, Grype) before they are published
information of KICS on a RUN of the Dockerfile of NPMplus, no security effect
volumes the services share by design (logs of nginx read by CrowdSec and the backend, the socket directory of the agent); each service mounts only its own subpath of the secrets volume
build stages that run on the build platform and produce files for every target platform (frontend, lego)
the reusable workflow security.yml of this repository called by its path, which pins it to the same commit
fuzzing through OSS-Fuzz or ClusterFuzzLite needs registering the project with an outside service; NginxionS registers nowhere
the OpenSSF badge needs registering the project at bestpractices.dev; NginxionS registers nowhere

not a token: the list of country codes of the flag icons, joined with dots (…SE.SG.SH.SI.SJ…), matches the SendGrid pattern of Trivy (SG. and 66 characters with dots)
cpnano is the command-line tool of the operator inside the container; the variable (the path of the agent's files) is set by whoever runs it, who can already read and write every file there
the request logging middleware logs only the headers it is given: X-Correlation-Id, X-Request-Id and X-Trace-Id (routers.go), ids of a request, no credential
the logs are JSON (openappsec.io/log: formatter -> json.Marshal), a value with a line break is escaped inside its string and cannot forge an entry
the lock key has every '/' replaced by '-' before it is joined to the lock directory: it names a file of that directory and nothing else (smartsync is not built into the image)

every path of the REST API goes through inRoot (filepath.Clean, then a prefix check against the root): '../' is refused, fileSystemDB_nginxions_test.go reads, writes and lists outside the root and fails

the values of the log query of a tuning event are SQL literals (sqlLiteral in pg/queries.go: quotes doubled, NUL removed; standard_conforming_strings); queries_nginxions_test.go checks a title that closes the quote
SHA-1 of an asset id only names its directory in the shared storage (the same name the agent uses), no integrity or secret depends on it
random jitter between retries of a request, not a secret or a token
